1	import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Invariants
2	
3	/-!
4	# Access kernel: conforming statics declarations and their numbering
5	
6	`StaticsConf` is the conformance of a statics declaration to §47 and §49 with no order between
7	identifiers. `StaticsOK` (`Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Invariants`) asks parents and owning statics to
8	be earlier statics; by §49 (last paragraph) this ordering only represents well-formedness. Every
9	conforming declaration has a consistent renumbering satisfying `StaticsOK`
10	(`StaticsConf.exists_renumber`), and every declaration satisfying `StaticsOK` conforms
11	(`StaticsConf.of_staticsOK`).
12	-/
13	
14	namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access
15	
16	/-! ## Conformance (§40, §47, §49) -/
17	
18	/-- Structural parent of static `i` (§40): `none` for a root static or an index outside the
19	declaration. -/
20	def staticParent (statics : Statics) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (statics[i]?).bind (·.1.1)
21	
22	/-- Owning static of static `i` (§40, §47): `none` for a static owned by frame 0 or an index
23	outside the declaration. -/
24	def staticOwner (statics : Statics) (i : Nat) : Option Nat := (statics[i]?).bind (·.1.2.1)
25	
26	/-- Conformance of a statics declaration to §47 and §49, with no order between identifiers
27	(§49, last paragraph). Owners are frame 0 or a static (§40, §47), parents and owning statics are
28	declared statics (§49.2, §49.3), composition links are acyclic (§49.2), no static is owned,
29	directly or transitively, by itself (§47), and every structural part has its parent's owner
30	(§49.2, §40).
31	
32	Acyclicity is the irreflexivity of the transitive closure `Relation.TransGen` of the one-step
33	link (`a`'s parent, resp. owning static, is `b`): `TransGen link i i` holds exactly when a
34	nonempty chain of links leads from `i` back to `i`, which is what §47 ("owned, directly or
35	transitively, by itself") and §49.2 (acyclic composition links) exclude. No bound on chain
36	length is involved. -/
37	structure StaticsConf (statics : Statics) : Prop where
38	  /-- §49.2: composition links are valid; every structural parent is a declared static. -/
39	  parent_lt : ∀ i p, staticParent statics i = some p → p < statics.length
40	  /-- §49.3, §47: owners are valid; every owning static is a declared static. -/
41	  owner_lt : ∀ i o, staticOwner statics i = some o → o < statics.length
42	  /-- §49.2: composition links are acyclic; no static is its own strict structural ancestor. -/
43	  parent_acyclic : ∀ i, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => staticParent statics a = some b) i i
44	  /-- §47: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. -/
45	  owner_acyclic : ∀ i, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => staticOwner statics a = some b) i i
46	  /-- §49.2, §40: every structural part shares its parent's owner. -/
47	  part_owner : ∀ i p, staticParent statics i = some p →
48	    staticOwner statics i = staticOwner statics p
49	
50	/-! ## Renumbering (§49, last paragraph; §63.2) -/
51	
52	/-- A static's entry with its references, parent and owning static, mapped through `τ`; its
53	kind and initial state are kept (§49, last paragraph). -/
54	def mapRefs (τ : Nat → Nat) (e : (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool) :
55	    (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool :=
56	  ((e.1.1.map τ, e.1.2.1.map τ, e.1.2.2), e.2)
57	
58	/-- Renumbering of a declaration by `σ` (§49, last paragraph): new index `i` holds old static
59	`σ[i]`, its parent and owning static mapped through the inverse `σ.idxOf`. Meant for `σ` a
60	permutation of `List.range statics.length`. -/
61	def renumber (σ : List Nat) (statics : Statics) : Statics :=
62	  σ.map fun j => mapRefs σ.idxOf ((statics[j]?).getD ((none, none, 0), false))
63	
64	/-- Consistent renumbering (§49, last paragraph; §63.2): the new index `σ.idxOf x` of every old
65	static `x` holds `x` with its parent and owning static mapped through `σ.idxOf`, and its kind and
66	initial state; the parts of every place keep their relative order, which is their positional
67	field order (§63.2; `kids` orders the parts of a place by index). -/
68	structure ConsistentRenumbering (σ : List Nat) (statics : Statics) : Prop where
69	  /-- Parents to parents, owning statics to owning statics, same kind and initial state. -/
70	  entry : ∀ x < statics.length,
71	    (renumber σ statics)[σ.idxOf x]? = (statics[x]?).map (mapRefs σ.idxOf)
72	  /-- §63.2: the field order of every place is preserved. -/
73	  field_order : ∀ x y p, staticParent statics x = some p → staticParent statics y = some p →
74	    x < y → σ.idxOf x < σ.idxOf y
75	
76	/-! ## Proof support: chains of a partial link -/
77	
78	/-- Pigeonhole: a duplicate-free list of numbers below `n` has at most `n` elements. -/
79	private theorem nodup_length_le : ∀ (n : Nat) (l : List Nat), l.Nodup → (∀ a ∈ l, a < n) →
80	    l.length ≤ n
81	  | 0, [], _, _ => Nat.le_refl _
82	  | 0, a :: _, _, h => absurd (h a (List.mem_cons_self ..)) (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
83	  | n + 1, l, hd, h => by
84	    have := nodup_length_le n (l.erase n) (hd.erase n) fun a ha => by
85	      rw [hd.mem_erase_iff] at ha
86	      have := h a ha.2
87	      omega
88	    rw [List.length_erase] at this
89	    split at this <;> omega
90	
91	/-- `k` links `f` from `x`. -/
92	private def iter (f : Nat → Option Nat) : Nat → Nat → Option Nat
93	  | 0, x => some x
94	  | k + 1, x => (iter f k x).bind f
95	
96	private theorem iter_add (f : Nat → Option Nat) (x i : Nat) : ∀ d,
97	    iter f (i + d) x = (iter f i x).bind (iter f d)
98	  | 0 => by
99	    show iter f i x = _
100	    cases iter f i x <;> rfl
101	  | d + 1 => by
102	    show (iter f (i + d) x).bind f = _
103	    rw [iter_add f x i d, Option.bind_assoc]
104	    rfl
105	
106	private theorem transGen_of_iter {f : Nat → Option Nat} {x : Nat} : ∀ {k y : Nat},
107	    iter f (k + 1) x = some y → Relation.TransGen (fun a b => f a = some b) x y
108	  | 0, _, h => .single h
109	  | k + 1, _, h => by
110	    obtain ⟨c, hc, hcy⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.1 h
111	    exact .tail (transGen_of_iter hc) hcy
112	
113	/-- An acyclic partial link whose targets are below `n` has chains of fewer than `n` links from
114	any `x < n`. -/
115	private theorem iter_bound {f : Nat → Option Nat} {n : Nat}
116	    (hacyc : ∀ a, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => f a = some b) a a)
117	    (hlt : ∀ a b, f a = some b → b < n) {x : Nat} (hx : x < n) {k : Nat}
118	    (hk : (iter f k x).isSome) : k < n := by
119	  let g := fun i => (iter f i x).getD 0
120	  have hsome : ∀ i ≤ k, iter f i x = some (g i) := by
121	    intro i hi
122	    have := iter_add f x i (k - i)
123	    rw [Nat.add_sub_cancel' hi] at this
124	    cases hc : iter f i x with
125	    | none => rw [hc] at this; rw [this] at hk; simp at hk
126	    | some c => simp [g, hc]
127	  have hlt' : ∀ a ∈ (List.range (k + 1)).map g, a < n := by
128	    intro a ha
129	    obtain ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.1 ha
130	    have hi' := hsome i (by rw [List.mem_range] at hi; omega)
131	    cases i with
132	    | zero => simp only [iter, Option.some.injEq] at hi'; omega
133	    | succ j =>
134	      obtain ⟨c, -, hc⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.1 hi'
135	      exact hlt c _ hc
136	  have hnd : ((List.range (k + 1)).map g).Nodup := by
137	    unfold List.Nodup
138	    rw [List.pairwise_map]
139	    refine List.pairwise_lt_range.imp_of_mem fun {i j} hi hj hij heq => ?_
140	    rw [List.mem_range] at hi hj
141	    have hj' := iter_add f x i (j - i)
142	    rw [Nat.add_sub_cancel' (Nat.le_of_lt hij), hsome i (by omega), hsome j (by omega), heq,
143	      Option.bind_some] at hj'
144	    obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ : ∃ d, j - i = d + 1 := ⟨j - i - 1, by omega⟩
145	    rw [hd] at hj'
146	    exact hacyc _ (transGen_of_iter hj'.symm)
147	  have := nodup_length_le n _ hnd hlt'
148	  simp only [List.length_map, List.length_range] at this
149	  omega
150	
151	/-- Length of the chain of links `f` from `x`, cut at `k` links. -/
152	private def chainLen (f : Nat → Option Nat) : Nat → Nat → Nat
153	  | 0, _ => 0
154	  | k + 1, x => match f x with
155	    | none => 0
156	    | some y => chainLen f k y + 1
157	
158	private theorem chainLen_some {f : Nat → Option Nat} {k x y : Nat} (h : f x = some y) :
159	    chainLen f (k + 1) x = chainLen f k y + 1 := by
160	  show (match f x with | none => 0 | some y => chainLen f k y + 1) = _
161	  rw [h]
162	
163	private theorem chainLen_congr {f : Nat → Option Nat} {x y : Nat} (h : f x = f y) :
164	    ∀ k, chainLen f k x = chainLen f k y
165	  | 0 => rfl
166	  | _ + 1 => by simp only [chainLen, h]
167	
168	private theorem iter_of_chainLen_ne {f : Nat → Option Nat} : ∀ {k z : Nat},
169	    chainLen f (k + 1) z ≠ chainLen f k z → (iter f (k + 1) z).isSome
170	  | 0, z, h => by
171	    cases hz : f z with
172	    | none => simp [chainLen, hz] at h
173	    | some y => simp [iter, hz]
174	  | k + 1, z, h => by
175	    cases hz : f z with
176	    | none => simp [chainLen, hz] at h
177	    | some y =>
178	      rw [chainLen_some hz, chainLen_some hz] at h
179	      have := iter_add f z 1 (k + 1)
180	      rw [Nat.add_comm 1] at this
181	      rw [this]
182	      simp only [iter, Option.bind_some, hz]
183	      exact iter_of_chainLen_ne (by omega)
184	
185	/-- Under an acyclic link with targets below `n`, the chain length cut at `n` grows by one along
186	each link. -/
187	private theorem chainLen_step {f : Nat → Option Nat} {n : Nat}
188	    (hacyc : ∀ a, ¬ Relation.TransGen (fun a b => f a = some b) a a)
189	    (hlt : ∀ a b, f a = some b → b < n) {x y : Nat} (h : f x = some y) :
190	    chainLen f n x = chainLen f n y + 1 := by
191	  have hy := hlt x y h
192	  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = m + 1 := ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
193	  rw [chainLen_some h]
194	  refine congrArg (· + 1) (Classical.byContradiction fun hne => ?_)
195	  have := iter_bound hacyc hlt hy (iter_of_chainLen_ne (k := m) (fun e => hne e.symm))
196	  omega
197	
198	/-! ## Proof support: the order of a conforming declaration -/
199	
200	/-- Ownership depth of a static. -/
201	private def odepth (statics : Statics) (x : Nat) : Nat :=
202	  chainLen (staticOwner statics) statics.length x
203	
204	/-- Structural depth of a static. -/
205	private def sdepth (statics : Statics) (x : Nat) : Nat :=
206	  chainLen (staticParent statics) statics.length x
207	
208	/-- Lexicographic order on (ownership depth, structural depth, index). -/
209	private def keyLe (statics : Statics) (a b : Nat) : Bool :=
210	  decide (odepth statics a < odepth statics b ∨ odepth statics a = odepth statics b ∧
211	    (sdepth statics a < sdepth statics b ∨ sdepth statics a = sdepth statics b ∧ a ≤ b))
212	
213	private theorem idxOf_lt_of_key {statics : Statics} {σ : List Nat}
214	    (hσ : σ.Perm (List.range statics.length)) (hs : σ.Pairwise (fun a b => keyLe statics a b))
215	    {x y : Nat} (hx : x < statics.length) (hy : y < statics.length)
216	    (hk : odepth statics x < odepth statics y ∨ odepth statics x = odepth statics y ∧
217	      (sdepth statics x < sdepth statics y ∨ sdepth statics x = sdepth statics y ∧ x < y)) :
218	    σ.idxOf x < σ.idxOf y := by
219	  have hix := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hσ.mem_iff.2 (List.mem_range.2 hx))
220	  have hiy := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (hσ.mem_iff.2 (List.mem_range.2 hy))
221	  have gx := List.getElem_idxOf hix
222	  have gy := List.getElem_idxOf hiy
223	  rcases Nat.lt_trichotomy (σ.idxOf x) (σ.idxOf y) with h | h | h
224	  · exact h
225	  · have : x = y := by
226	      rw [← gx, ← gy]
227	      exact getElem_congr rfl h hix
228	    subst this
229	    omega
230	  · have := List.pairwise_iff_getElem.1 hs _ _ hiy hix h
231	    rw [gx, gy] at this
232	    simp only [keyLe, decide_eq_true_eq] at this
233	    omega
234	
235	private theorem lt_of_parent {statics : Statics} {x p : Nat}
236	    (h : staticParent statics x = some p) : x < statics.length := by
237	  unfold staticParent at h
238	  cases hx : statics[x]? with
239	  | none => rw [hx] at h; cases h
240	  | some _ => exact (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 hx).1
241	
242	private theorem lt_of_owner {statics : Statics} {x o : Nat}
243	    (h : staticOwner statics x = some o) : x < statics.length := by
244	  unfold staticOwner at h
245	  cases hx : statics[x]? with
246	  | none => rw [hx] at h; cases h
247	  | some _ => exact (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 hx).1
248	
249	private theorem shape_parent (statics : Statics) (i : Nat) :
250	    ((statics.map (·.1))[i]?).bind (·.1) = staticParent statics i := by
251	  simp only [List.getElem?_map, staticParent]
252	  cases statics[i]? <;> rfl
253	
254	private theorem shape_owner (statics : Statics) (i : Nat) :
255	    ((statics.map (·.1))[i]?).bind (·.2.1) = staticOwner statics i := by
256	  simp only [List.getElem?_map, staticOwner]
257	  cases statics[i]? <;> rfl
258	
259	private theorem renumber_get {σ : List Nat} {statics : Statics} {i : Nat} (hi : i < σ.length)

# ERN — Memory Model Specification v0.1

**Edition v0.1 — corrective candidate, not yet validated**

Modified clauses, relative to v0 (each change is justified by a defect found while formalizing v0):

- §36: `MetaRight` governs authorities over existing storage, not the fresh allocation of `alloc`; §36 and §71.2 contradicted each other.
- §40: `RootHeld` restricted to usable root places, as in §49.7; the two clauses differed on unusable root places.
- §47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; a static ownership cycle made §57 false in the initial state.
- §51: a valid origin is an active origin; "valid" was undefined there.
- §57: definition of I5, which v0 named without defining.
- §59: "access operations" are O9–O11; read as all operations, §59 contradicted §69.
- §60.1: a valid origin chain is an active one, read through §44.
- §63.4: the active derived authorities covering the source from outside are named, and the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right are exempt; without this exemption no value could be moved through a derived authority.
- §63.9 (new): the destination is usable in the resulting state; without it an accepted transfer could create an ownership cycle and break §49.8 and §57.
- §69.2 and §70.3: the same exemption as §63.4, and rejection when an authority made inactive by the step keeps an active descendant; without it an accepted step left an active authority with an inactive origin.
- §71.2: the provider is a usable place; v0 did not require it to exist.
- §74 and §75: each `pin` installs an obligation of fresh identity and `unpin` ends one designated obligation; per-leaf pin flags let an `unpin` lift a pin installed by another `pin`.
- §76.6: the reading of the precondition (whole kernel state, `ArenaInv` of the new entry, resulting state); v0 admitted several readings with different verdicts.
- §78.3: restricted to anchors covering a leaf of the administered storage; as written, its second sentence was false.
- §82.2: address and provenance of a pointer to a region whose leaves all have zero physical size; v0 decided no address for that region.
- §86: the last sentence is rewritten; as written, it was false, since `reset` and `issue` leave a recycled leaf `Init` and readable.

**Higher normative authority:** *ERN — Language Charter v0* (October 27, 2026).  
This specification defines the normative rules of ERN's memory model. Technical names (`derive`, `transfer`, `issue`, etc.) designate **abstract semantic operations**; they do not constitute syntax decisions.

## Validation and Revision Procedure

This edition is a corrective candidate, not yet validated; it acquires normative authority under the ERN Charter v0 only once validated. Any subsequent semantic change must identify the clauses concerned, justify the change, and preserve the guarantees of the ERN Charter v0. Formal models and proofs are instruments for verifying this specification, not sources of additional rules. Behaviors not determined within its scope are explicitly identified.

------
The components described below constitute the logical state of the sequential discipline. They prescribe neither generalized runtime metadata nor reference syntax.

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

`F` is a nonempty stack of identified, non-duplicate frames. Every frame except the initial frame knows its parent. Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places. The **current frame** is at the top of the stack. `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` means `f₁` is `f₂` or an ancestor of `f₂` in the stack and its call chain.

The base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never exits. An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active. Frames have semantic existence; no particular runtime representation is required.

## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every **usable** root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The ownership graph of statics is acyclic: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

/-! ## `NoOrphan` (§54) -/

/-- One link of a `NoOrphan` chain (§54): `a` is active and structurally covers every leaf of the
place holding `b`. -/
def CoversHolder (s : S3) (a b : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[b]?) (fun z => match z.holder with
    | .place q => s.Active a ∧ ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, l ∈ s.afp a
    | .frame _ => False) False

/-- Consecutive elements of a list are related by `R` (§54, chains of `NoOrphan`). -/
def Linked (R : Nat → Nat → Prop) : List Nat → Prop
  | a :: b :: c => R a b ∧ Linked R (b :: c)
  | _ => True

/-- `NoOrphan` (§54): every active authority held by a place ends a finite, non-repeating chain of
authorities whose first link is active and held by a frame of the stack, each link covering the
whole place holding the next. -/
def NoOrphan (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority) (q : Nat), s.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
    ∃ (a₀ : Nat) (z : Authority) (f : Nat) (c : List Nat), s.A[a₀]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧
      z.holder = .frame f ∧ f ∈ s.F ∧ (a₀ :: c).Nodup ∧ (a₀ :: c).getLast? = some x ∧
      Linked (CoversHolder s) (a₀ :: c)

/-! ## Initial state (§47) -/

/-- Declared static storage (§47): each element is (parent, owning static, kind) with its
initial state, `true` for `Init` and `false` for `Uninit` (read on leaves only). -/
abbrev Statics := List ((Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool)

/-- Well-formed statics declaration (§47: the ownership graph of statics is acyclic; §49, last
paragraph: the ordering of identifiers represents this well-foundedness, and that of structural
parents): parents and owning statics are earlier statics, and a part has its parent's owning
static (§49.2). -/
def StaticsOK (statics : Statics) : Prop := ShapeOK 0 (statics.map (·.1))

/-- Decidability of `StaticsOK` (§47). -/
instance (statics : Statics) : Decidable (StaticsOK statics) := by
  unfold StaticsOK; infer_instance

/-- `S3.init statics` (§47): base frame 0 and the declared statics, owned by frame 0 or by
another static; one root `Modify` authority with no origin per root static, held by its owner;
leaves `Init` or `Uninit` as declared; no anchor, no derived authority, nothing dead, no
dynamic pinning obligation. -/
def S3.init (statics : Statics) : S3 :=
  { F := [0]
    nF := 1
    P := shapeP [] (.frame 0) (statics.map (·.1))
    I := fun l => if ((statics[l]?).map (·.2)).getD false then .init else .uninit
    A := (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))).map fun i =>
      ⟨.modify, none, footprint (shapeP [] (.frame 0) (statics.map (·.1))) i,
        shapeOwner (statics.map (·.1)) (.frame 0) i, true⟩
    D := fun _ => []
    dead := fun _ => false
    pins := [] }

/-- `StaticPinnedBottom` (§75, §80): every static place whose leaf is designated by `K.Pinned` is
directly owned by the base frame 0. A condition on `(K, statics)`. -/
def StaticPinnedBottom (k : K) (statics : Statics) : Prop :=
  ∀ l < statics.length, k.Pinned l →
    OptP ((S3.init statics).P[l]?) (fun pl => pl.owner = .frame 0) False

/-! ## Reachability (§57) -/

/-- States reachable from `S3.init statics` under the kernel steps O1–O16 (§57). -/
inductive Reachable (k : K) (statics : Statics) : S3 → Prop where
  | init : Reachable k statics (S3.init statics)
  | step {s s' : S3} : Reachable k statics s → KStep k s s' → Reachable k statics s'

/-! ## Non-vacuity examples (§47, §60–§75)

Each operation has an accepting state, decided by `decide` on concrete states built from
`S3.init`; a few rejections are included. -/

namespace Examples

/-- Test contract (§48): nothing declared disjoint or pinned, every leaf `SharedMutable`, every
external use done, every place deallocable, every request satisfiable. -/
def K0 : K := ⟨fun _ _ => False, fun _ => True, fun _ => False, fun _ => True, fun _ => True,
  fun _ _ => True, fun _ _ _ => True⟩

/-- Decidability of `K0.DeclaredDisjoint` (§48). -/
-----
/-- A local shape as a shape whose elements have no owning element (§71.1, §72: locals and
allocated storage are owned by the receiving holder). -/
def LocalShape.toShape (ls : LocalShape) : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) :=
  ls.map fun e => (e.1, none, e.2)

/-- Owner of element `i` of a shape (§47, §72, §71): its owning element if any, `hd`
otherwise. -/
def shapeOwner (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) (hd : Holder) (i : Nat) : Holder :=
  match (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) with
  | some o => .place o
  | none => hd

/-- Places `P` followed by the elements of a shape (§47, §71, §72): (parent, owning element,
kind), owned by their owning element or by `hd`. -/
def shapeP (P : List Place) (hd : Holder) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) :
    List Place :=
  P ++ (List.range ls.length).map fun i =>
    ⟨(ls[i]?).bind (·.1), shapeOwner ls hd i, ((ls[i]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩

/-- Well-formed shape at offset `n` (§72.2, §71.1; for statics, the hypothesis recorded for
§47): the parent and the owning element of an element are earlier elements, and a part has the
owning element of its parent. -/
def ShapeOK (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i ∈ List.range ls.length,
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)) (fun r => n ≤ r ∧ r < n + i ∧
      (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) = (ls[r - n]?).bind (·.2.1)) True ∧
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1)) (fun o => n ≤ o ∧ o < n + i) True

/-- Decidability of `ShapeOK` (§72.2, §71.1). -/
instance (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Decidable (ShapeOK n ls) := by
  unfold ShapeOK; infer_instance

/-- Indices of the root elements (no parent) of a shape (§40 root places; §47, §71, §72). -/
def rootIdx (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : List Nat :=
  (List.range ls.length).filter fun i => ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)).isNone

/-! ## O6 `enterFrame` (§72) -/

/-- Places after `enterFrame` (§72, `ok` effect): the locals appended, owned by the new frame. -/
def enterP (s : S3) (ls : LocalShape) : List Place := shapeP s.P (.frame s.nF) ls.toShape

/-- Effect of `enterFrame(params, locals)` (§72, `ok` effect): a new frame `nF` is pushed; the
parameters are now held by it; locals are appended (uninitialized, no anchor, alive) with one
active root `Modify` authority per root local, held by the new frame; pinning obligations are
unchanged. -/
def enterEff (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : S3 :=

/-- Current frame, the top of the stack (§39). -/
def S3.top (s : S3) : Nat := s.F.headD 0

/-! ## Decidable helpers -/

/-- Predicate on an optional value, `P y` for `some y` and `d` for `none`; used to read the
components of `S3` (§38). -/
def OptP {α : Type} (o : Option α) (P : α → Prop) (d : Prop) : Prop :=
  match o with
  | some y => P y
  | none => d

/-- Decidability of `OptP` (§38). -/
instance {α : Type} (o : Option α) (P : α → Prop) (d : Prop) [DecidablePred P] [Decidable d] :
    Decidable (OptP o P d) :=
  match o with
  | some y => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (P y))
  | none => inferInstanceAs (Decidable d)

## 63. O4 — Consuming Value Transfer

**Preconditions**

1. `source` and `destination` are usable, and the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over their relevant footprints.
2. Source and destination have the **same shape of ordered subtrees**. The `i`-th child of each source part corresponds to the `i`-th child of the corresponding destination part; all nodes are matched. Structural field identity is positional, not an arbitrary matching of children.
3. **All** source leaves are `Init`, and **no** destination leaf is `Init`. The source and destination footprints are disjoint.
4. No exclusive authority is duplicated; validity of derived authorities and active projections is preserved. No active derived authority held outside `source` covers a source leaf, except the authorities through which the step exercises its `Modify` right over `source`: the exercisable authority on which that right rests and its origin chain. Other active authorities remain subject to this check. Authorities held by parts of `source` are transferred with the value and are controlled by §63.8.
5. **No in-place source leaf is pinned**, either statically (`K.Pinned`) or dynamically (`pin`). Storage merely **owned** by the source, which is not itself moved by the transfer of that value, does not prevent this transfer.
6. Dependencies of all still-usable places following the value remain valid; non-escape constraints and `AnchorOrder` are checked in the **resulting state**, including transferred anchors of owned places that remain usable.
7. All moved held authorities, including those of owned storage, satisfy `AnchorOrderHeld` in the resulting state; no authority may escape a local anchor on the grounds that its containing value was transferred.
8. **Local self-blocking prevention:** For each active authority held before the step by a part `r` of `source` whose holder becomes the corresponding part `corr(r)` of `destination`, that authority's footprint contains **no leaf** of `corr(r)` in the resulting state. Transfer is rejected if this local check fails; no global authority-acyclicity check is imposed.
9. **Destination usability:** `destination` is usable in the resulting state.

**`ok` effect:**

- every source leaf becomes `Moved` and each corresponding destination leaf becomes `Init`;
- every authority held by source part `r` acquires as its new holder the corresponding destination part `corr(r)`, not indiscriminately the destination root;
- places owned by `r` become owned by `corr(r)`; their roots follow this owner according to `RootHeld`;
- value dependencies follow the corresponding places under validity guarantees; no authority is created or duplicated;
- destination places receive the transferred values and rights without automatically moving storage not owned by a source part.

**Other outcome:** `reject`. `transfer` to a call result is subject to these same rules.

A partially initialized structure may be transferred **field by field**, but only for fields individually eligible for transfer. This does not automatically destructure a value that owns storage **at the container level**: that storage stays with the container if the container is not transferred. Conversion between structures with permuted fields must be handled separately, not as a `transfer`.

## 64. O5 — Explicit Attachment of an Anchor

/-- Decidability of `partOf` (§40). -/
instance (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Decidable (partOf P p q) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- Leaf (§40): a place with no structural child. -/
def isLeaf (P : List Place) (l : Nat) : Prop := ∀ r < P.length, parentOf P r ≠ some l

/-- Decidability of `isLeaf` (§40). -/
instance (P : List Place) (l : Nat) : Decidable (isLeaf P l) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ _, _))

/-- `footprint(q)` (§40): the leaves of `P` that are parts of `q`. -/
def footprint (P : List Place) (q : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range P.length).filter fun l => decide (isLeaf P l ∧ partOf P l q)

/-- Two places overlap when their footprints share a leaf (§63.3). -/
def overlap (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Prop := ∃ l ∈ footprint P p, l ∈ footprint P q

/-- Decidability of `overlap` (§63.3). -/
instance (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Decidable (overlap P p q) :=

- **No stronger or weaker reading of "owned".** Read broadly, "owned" can mean owned by a part of oneself, as in `OwnedIn`, or reached through a cycle that mixes parent and owner links. Under `part_owner`, any such cycle reduces to a pure owner-link cycle: owner(a_{k+1}) = owner(b_k), so the b_k form an owner cycle.
